title: GLM as a named three-piece machine
dek: Wikipedia GLM: random component, linear predictor, link. Canonical links and IRLS already have Simplfy plates.
story: Wikipedia's Generalized linear model page is the three-piece slogan: an exponential-family random part, η = Xβ, and a link g(μ) = η. Nelder & Wedderburn 1972 is the citation, not the ingested text.
stats-glm-link already insists the linear predictor is not the mean. stats-exponential-family already owns A(η). stats-iwls is the algorithm. This card is the encyclopedia assembly drawing.
Quasi-likelihood is a cousin that keeps the mean–variance map without a full density — own plate. Do not smuggle it in as 'still a GLM' without saying so.
deep: Canonical link is a convenience, not a moral law (probit exists).
Offsets belong in η, frozen coefficient 1.
Binary, count, and positive continuous outcomes are different random components.
TB DST Bernoulli GLMs are the usual worked example on child plates.

visual.caption: Three pieces stacked. Each piece already has a deeper Simplfy plate.
visual.annotation: Quasi-likelihood drops the full density and keeps V(μ).
